subject: Partner Q&A: regional storage & deletion controls for Vertex Analytics marketplace listing
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@vertexanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Ops <aws-partner-ops@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on regional storage controls for Redwood marketplace listing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move toward the marketplace listing we need to align on a few specific items around where our customer data will be stored and how deletion/retention will be handled across AWS/GCP/Azure. Can you confirm the following for the Vertex listing?

1) For a US region listing, do you support hard region-locking so data never leaves the selected cloud region (e.g., us-west-2, us-east-1)?
2) What are the retention defaults for audit logs vs. request/response payloads? Can we configure shorter retention for payloads for compliance?
3) Do you provide a programmatic deletion API (per-account or per-tenant) plus an SLA for propagation to object stores and caches?
4) How long are KV cache artifacts or ephemeral runtime artifacts kept after a delete request?
5) Will Redwood provide attestations or an appendix (SOC2/Marketplace controls) stating storage jurisdiction per marketplace listing?

I attached a short list of questions (Vertex_Qs_v1.pdf) to make review easier. If you can send a mapping matrix for AWS/GCP/Azure that shows where artifacts live and the deletion pathway, that would be perfect.

We'd like to close this before the marketplace contract redlines stage.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Cloud Security
Vertex Analytics

Attachment: Vertex_Qs_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@vertexanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Ops <aws-partner-ops@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on regional storage controls for Redwood marketplace listing

Maya —

Appreciate the detail. Short answers up front, then next steps.

1) Region locking: Yes — Redwood supports region locking at the tenancy level for marketplace listings. For hosted listings we pin object-store and compute to the chosen region (we use native cloud objects: S3/GCS/Blob). If you opt for Dedicated/Private we can support additional contractual guarantees.

2) Retention defaults: Audit logs (control-plane traces + token-level usage) default to 180 days. Request/response payloads default to 30 days and can be lowered to 7 days on a per-account policy for marketplace partners (subject to PR and listed config).

3) Deletion API & SLA: We expose a per-tenant deletion API that enqueues TTL and immediate purge operations. Propagation SLA: typical propagation to object store is within 24 hours, KV cache eviction within 15 minutes; we provide a compliance report within 72 hours showing purge events.

4) KV cache artifacts: Ephemeral runtime KV entries are removed on eviction; for customers who request deletion we flush session caches immediately and mark related cache keys for GC; full purge is typically completed within 15 minutes to 4 hours depending on workload.

5) Attestations: We can provide a marketplace appendix that maps listing -> storage jurisdiction and includes a SOC2-friendly statement. Marissa (cc) will attach the deletion playbook summary and a simple matrix.

I'll attach a working matrix (redwood-marketplace-data-matrix.xlsx) and loop in our marketplace/program ops to confirm any additional contract language. Proposed next step: Kar + Marissa can prepare a mutual action plan with explicit mapping rows for AWS/GCP/Azure and proposed contract language.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-marketplace-data-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@vertexanalytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on regional storage controls for Redwood marketplace listing

Hi Maya — adding some technical specifics to Karthik's summary so your security team has concrete mappings.

- Object storage: For AWS listings we use customer-linked S3 buckets that Redwood either provisions or references; GCP uses GCS, Azure uses Blob Storage. Data-at-rest encryption uses customer-managed keys where requested (KMS/HSM options available on Dedicated/Private).
- Model artifacts vs. customer payloads: Model weights are stored in read-only model registries; customer payloads (inputs/outputs) are stored in tenant-scoped buckets with region tags.
- Cache and KV: We maintain an in-memory KV cache across the serving fleet for latency; KV snapshots (for checkpointing) are written to region-scoped object storage and follow the same retention policy as payloads.
- Deletion playbook: On delete request we (1) mark tenant for immediate cache eviction, (2) schedule object-store deletion with version-safe sweep, (3) run a background integrity job to ensure no orphaned artifacts. For marketplace listings we provide a summary PDF that can be attached to the contract.

Attached: deletion-playbook-summary.pdf (short one-pager) — let me know if you need a formal appendix template.

Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: deletion-playbook-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks for the summary. A couple of notes from the AWS marketplace side:

- For listings that claim region-locking we will require a per-listing appendix that specifies service endpoints and storage regions.
- We also require a mapping table that shows what artifact types live in which region and retention windows; this is reviewed during listing verification.
- If you want us to display "US-only storage" on the listing it needs to be backed by the contractual appendix and validated during the security review.

Can you provide the mapping table as a CSV and the proposed appendix language by EOB Wednesday 07 Apr so we can schedule the marketplace validation?

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Partner Ops
